text:
Maya (Support): Hey team, customer 'VoiceVia' reporting ~30% of inference API calls failing with 502/504 in eu-west-1 since last cert rotation. They see TLS handshake timeouts at our gateway and several 502s from custapi. Logs attached from their side show timeout waiting for upstream.

Sam (SRE): Can you paste a sample request id / edge node? Any pattern (client IP, model)?

Maya (Support): Request ids: r-0a3b9c, r-0a3b9f, r-0a3ba1 — all from our edge in eu-west-1a. Model: text-gen-large. No consistent client IP, variety of customers. Happens across SDKs and curl. Customer ran openssl s_client and got handshake timeout: 'connect:errno=110'.

Lena (CS): Customer is annoyed, says it started right after our scheduled cert rotation last night at 02:12 UTC. They tried fallback region (us-east-1) and those calls succeed.

Priya (Network): Noted. I'm seeing spikes in DNS SERVFAILs from 2 of our transit resolvers around the same time as the rotation. Also some large EDNS responses from authoritative returning 1400+ bytes which leads to UDP truncation. Some resolvers fall back to TCP, but our edge has a short DNS tcp timeout.

Diego (Runtime Eng): Interesting. If DNS falls back to TCP but connection stalls, the gateway might try to open TLS to a non-responsive upstream and hit handshake timeout. Do we have any stack traces from the edge?

Maya (Support): Pasting edge log excerpt: 

```
[2026-03-12T02:13:07Z] edge-eu-west-1a - req r-0a3b9c - upstream connect 10.4.2.11:443 error: handshake timeout
[2026-03-12T02:13:07Z] connpool - dial tcp 10.4.2.11:443: connection timed out
[2026-03-12T02:13:07Z] proxy - returning 502 to client
```

Priya (Network): I ran a diag from edge host: 

```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 api.internal.voicevia.redwood  ; returns 1.2.3.4 (ok)
$ dig +dnssec @1.1.1.1 api.internal.voicevia.redwood ; large answer, UDP truncated (TC flag set)
$ dig +tcp @1.1.1.1 api.internal.voicevia.redwood ; times out after 3s
```

Sam (SRE): That 3s TCP DNS timeout is bad. Our resolver pool has mixed behavior: some providers allow TCP, some throttle or drop. If edge DNS fails to resolve timely, it may use stale cache or error, the routing may pick an incompatible IP (or none) and then handshake fails.

Diego (Runtime Eng): Also check SNI / cert chain length. During rotation we pushed a new intermediate which increased DNS TXT/CAA records? Joking, but long chains combined with MTU issues can cause TCP fallback oddities. More likely the resolver UDP truncation -> TCP fallback failing is the root.

Priya (Network): Verified MTU on path is 1500, but EDNS reported 4096 from authoritative which triggers fragmentation/truncation in some networks. Some transit providers block fragmented DNS packets.

Maya (Support): Customer provided their traces showing curl with --verbose: 

```
*   Trying 10.4.2.11:443...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect timeout after 5000ms
* Closing connection 0
* Received HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

Lena (CS): Customer asks for ETA and mitigation. They asked if we can route their traffic to a pinned region temporarily.

Sam (SRE): Short-term mitigations: 1) Add an emergency DNS fallback to our internal cached resolver (route through our resolver-cache cluster) for impacted edges. 2) Increase DNS TCP timeout on edge hosts to 10s. 3) Roll forward an edge config to prefer cached IPs when TCP DNS fails instead of immediate error.

Diego (Runtime Eng): For longer term: 1) Harden resolver pool (disallow resolvers that throttle TCP). 2) Force EDNS buffer size to 1232 on queries to avoid fragmentation. 3) Add explicit retry path: if TLS handshake times out, retry after re-resolving with +tcp. 4) Tune TLS handshake deadline a bit (but careful with latency SLO).

Priya (Network): I can push a filter to our authoritative to advertise EDNS 1232 and disable sending large UDP responses where not needed. Also will add healthcheck probes to resolvers to detect TCP-blocking behavior.

Maya (Support): Quick repro steps for SRE: 
1) From an edge node, run: `dig +short api.internal.voicevia.redwood @<resolver>` and `dig +tcp api.internal.voicevia.redwood @<resolver>`
2) curl with --resolve pointing to the returned IP and observe connect timeouts
3) tail edge logs for req ids above

Sam (SRE): I'll deploy the DNS TCP timeout bump to the canary edges in eu-west-1 now. Also adding a temporary route rule for the customer's org-id to prefer us-east-1.

certbot-bot: Deployed cert rotation canary to eu-west-1a at 02:12 UTC :white_check_mark:

Diego (Runtime Eng): One code note: current dialer uses a 2s network resolve->dial window. If DNS fallback to TCP is happening it can exceed that. Increasing to 6s should reduce false positives but we must monitor tail latency.

Lena (CS): I'll message VoiceVia with mitigation steps and offer usage credit. Please keep me posted so I can close the escalation after monitoring.

Priya (Network): Initial changes pushed: authoritative EDNS max-size clamped to 1232, resolver healthcheck script added. Monitoring for 30m.

Sam (SRE): Canary rollout of DNS TCP timeout -> 10s applied to 5% edges at 02:46 UTC. Early results: customer request failures dropped from 30% -> 4% on canary nodes. Rolling to 30% now. :thumbsup:

Maya (Support): VoiceVia confirmed retries are working and error rate down. They still saw a handful of 504s but much improved.

Diego (Runtime Eng): Action items: 
- runtime: implement re-resolve-on-handshake-timeout (PR 2741)
- infra: block resolvers that fail TCP in autoscaler (ticket NET-512)
- ops: add temporary org-route to us-east-1 for VoiceVia until DNS cache full roll completes

Lena (CS): Customer notified, offering 10% credit for downtime window. They appreciated the quick response.

Maya (Support): Closing loop: keep monitoring 24h, then revert temporary routing. Great cross-team work.

Sam (SRE): Marking incident as mitigated, will open a follow-up postmortem for the cert rotation + DNS interaction (assigning Sam, Priya, Diego).

Priya (Network): I'll attach resolver traces, mtr and tcpdump samples to the postmortem.

Maya (Support): Thanks all.
